The function is kept alive solely by the test `test_review_isolation_rejection_line_drops_unknown_tokens`.
  WHY: Does not cause a runtime failure. It is dead production code that future readers may mistake for live code and attempt to modify or maintain.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:2287-2288 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The conflict resolver's regex at line 2287 has been extended to accept the new `category=` and `depth=` format (so the diagnostic source is validated), but the reason extraction on line 2288 (`${BASH_REMATCH[1]%% *}`) strips the category and depth, reporting only `reason=unsafe_directory`. Same pattern in `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:170-171`.
  WHY: Does not cause a runtime failure — the full diagnostic with category and depth is already present in the helper's own `::error::` line. These downstream callers use the reason token only to classify the failure (e.g. `transfer_rollback_failed` vs `unsafe_directory`), and `unsafe_directory` is sufficient for that classification decision. The category/depth serve the workflow-failure-heal fingerprint and the operator log, both of which read the helper's original `::error::` line, not these downstream echoes. This is an intentional backward-compatible design, not a defect.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:2287-2290 (the regex on 2287 and the resolver_transfer_reason assignment on 2288 followed by the echo on 2290) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: After the regex is widened to accept `unsafe_directory ... category=<class> depth=<1|2|3+>`, the assignment `resolver_transfer_reason=" reason=${BASH_REMATCH[1]%% *}"` truncates at the first space, leaving only `reason=unsafe_directory`. The echoed error on line 2290 therefore still reports just `reason=unsafe_directory` to the workflow log, exactly the regression the new format was added to fix for this caller.
  WHY: When the integration-sync resolver aborts because the editor created an excluded directory, the workflow log and the autofix-failure fingerprint lose the rule class. Operators investigating the rejection see only `unsafe_directory` and have to fall back on the archived `editor_attempt_*.err`, exactly what the stable-side change was supposed to avoid for this call site.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:168-173 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Mirror of the resolver defect. The widened regex on line 170 captures the full `unsafe_directory category=<class> depth=<n>` string into `${BASH_REMATCH[1]}`, but the assignment on line 171 (`rb_transfer_reason=" reason=${BASH_REMATCH[1]%% *}"`) truncates at the first space, so the echoed error on line 173 reports only `reason=unsafe_directory`. Same fix the apply-fixes path got; the review-blocked judge path did not.
  WHY: A `close_and_reissue` / `fix` judge verdict whose sandbox transfer was refused for a `dot_github_subtree` / `excluded_name_variant` / etc. directory will not surface that classification in the workflow log; only the bare `reason=unsafe_directory` reaches `gh run view --log-failed` and the workflow-failure-heal intake fingerprint.
- changelog.d/6413-review-sandbox-transfer-reject-diagnostics.md and changelog.d/6424-review-sandbox-unsafe-directory-category.md:both fragments added in this PR | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Two fragments describe the same observable change (the new `category=` / `depth=` diagnostic and its archiving) from slightly different angles. CLAUDE.md §20.A requires exactly one fragment per PR when the PR changes observable behaviour; a release assembly folds both and produces overlapping release notes.
  WHY: At release time `scripts/assemble_changelog.py` runs once per consumer; two fragments for one fix double-print under both `Fixed` and `Changed` headings and force the user to scan two near-identical bullets to understand what changed.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:62-68 (definition of _log_safe_dir) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: After `main()` switched from `f" dir={_log_safe_dir(exc.rejected_dir)}"` to `f" category={exc.category} depth={exc.depth}"`, `_log_safe_dir` is no longer reachable from any production code path. Only `tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py::test_review_isolation_rejection_line_drops_unknown_tokens` still imports and exercises it, so the helper is a tested-but-dead function: future readers may mistake it for live code and reintroduce a path-leaking `dir=` token.
  WHY: A future fix that adds `_log_safe_dir` back into a code path reopens the path-leak the change was supposed to close, and the test that exercises it would happily pass, hiding the regression.
- tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py:~8781-8815 (`_review_isolation_transfer_case` helper) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The helper sets `REVIEW_SANDBOX_TRANSFER_REASON_FILE` in the subprocess environment and then reads back `reason_file`, but `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py` does not read that environment variable — the only producer of the file is the wrapper `scripts/review_untrusted_sandbox.sh` (lines 351 and 448), which the helper bypasses by calling the Python helper directly. Every `assert reason is None` is therefore vacuously true regardless of the sandbox outcome; the env-var plumbing is dead.
  WHY: The new tests do not actually exercise the reason-file path they are named after. If a future change stops writing the file (or stops honouring the env var name), these tests still pass and the regression would only surface via the apply-fixes archive check, which is a weaker signal.
